definitions.explanation: Describes someone whose conduct and manners are proper and refined.

examples.japanese: あの{子|こ}は{行儀|ぎょうぎ}がいい。
{行儀|ぎょうぎ}よく{座|すわ}りなさい。
{食事中|しょくじちゅう}は{行儀|ぎょうぎ}よくするように{親|おや}に{言|い}われて{育|そだ}った。
examples.english: I was raised being told by my parents to behave properly during meals.

notes:
{行儀|ぎょうぎ} means manners or conduct, particularly at the table or in social situations. The full expression {行儀|ぎょうぎ}が{良|よ}い describes someone whose behavior meets social standards. Often used about children. The adverbial form {行儀|ぎょうぎ}よく (properly, with good manners) is very common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {行儀|ぎょうぎ}よく{食|た}べる: to eat with good manners
- {行儀|ぎょうぎ}よく{座|すわ}る: to sit properly
- {行儀|ぎょうぎ}が{悪|わる}い: ill-mannered, badly behaved
- お{行儀|ぎょうぎ}: manners (with polite prefix, often used with children)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {礼儀正|れいぎただ}しい: polite, courteous — focuses on formal politeness and social etiquette
- {品|ひん}がいい: elegant, refined — emphasizes class and sophistication
- {躾|しつけ}がいい: well-disciplined — focuses on upbringing and training
- マナーがいい: to have good manners — loanword equivalent, often used in public/social contexts
